title: kerberos: TGT as an identity claim
description:
No module. SPEC-HIRE lists it Day-Two: a valid TGT from klist, the Kerberos principal as the identity claim.

WORTH MORE THAN ITS DAY-TWO PLACEMENT SUGGESTS. Kerberos is the identity substrate of the enterprise and DoD environments where the CAC/PIV work (persona-qbnm's piv child) and the high-security scenario on persona-3tly actually live. A site running CAC is running Kerberos. It is also the system README names as the nearest prior art that 'stops at one identity source, no presence model' -- so consuming it rather than competing with it is the more honest position.

Also the reason the clock-skew question is moot in these environments, recorded on persona-3tly.7: Kerberos will not function without synchronised clocks, so any site with a TGT has enforced time sync.

SHAPE PROBLEM, same family as tailscale and oidc: a TGT is a bearer credential. klist reports what the cache holds; it does not sign the daemon's challenge. There IS a real path here that the others lack -- Kerberos has actual challenge-response machinery, so proof could mean obtaining a service ticket rather than reading the cache. Decide which before implementing, and see persona-ux32.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision on whether proof means reading the cache or exercising Kerberos; if the former, the trust basis is calibrated per persona-ux32 rather than assumed.
